title: Reactance of L and C Explained Simply | PUC Electronics Class 11
description:
Aarav opens an old speaker box. The tiny speaker plays only the high notes, and the only part in its path is a capacitor. How can one small part sort sound by pitch? The answer is reactance: the opposition of a coil or a capacitor to alternating current, measured in ohms.

On a live breadboard we turn up the frequency through a 0.1 H coil and watch the current fall, then swap in a 10 microfarad capacitor and watch it rise, while the oscilloscope shows the current lagging the voltage by 90 degrees in the coil and leading it in the capacitor. We derive XL = 2 pi f L and XC = 1/(2 pi f C) step by step from the slope of the wave, plot both against frequency, see why a coil is a plain wire for DC and a capacitor blocks DC, and work out the current of a 10 microfarad capacitor on the 230 V, 50 Hz mains. Then the exam trap (XC falls as frequency rises), where it is asked, an original JEE Main pattern practice question with a full solution, and a formula card to screenshot.

This is Episode 15 of PUC Electronics, Class 11, Chapter 2: Principles of Electricity, Network Theorems and AC Principles (Karnataka PUC Electronics).
